items.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: I was actually around backstage at some Benny Goodman concerts with Urbie Green and Benny and Bucky Pizzarelli and Hank and all those people, just as a kid

ctx.x: Well that explains I think partly one of your answers early on today with the sociology and the musicology. And I can also see why you spend so much preparation time with your jazz history class, not to just start out with a person, okay here we go, Louis Armstrong and move forward.

And understanding who Nick Payton is. You know what I mean. Or who Wynton Marsalis is. Or whom you are or I am or any of these people are. When you start to put it in that context. So that happened in those years. And then in the meantime I had mentioned Russ Connor before and BG on the Record and the Benny Goodman biodiscography. So I had been very much pursuing that stuff too, collecting records, and I was doing radio shows in college and all this kind of stuff, like a lot of us did. And because I knew Hank…

kid in New York you know, who you know is always collecting your records. Maybe he might know. And he’s a musician. So I left school. I don’t have a bachelor’s degree. I’m one of the rare people who wound up teaching in the master’s — I taught in the graduate school of the school I never graduated from, which I guess you can’t do anymore, right?
